findings.where: shiploop_navigator.py `_skill_call_gate`, called only in the Improve import branch of `complete`; plan steps 6.2 and 6.3 (`improve-pass`); shiploop_keepalive.py `skill_gate`
findings.observation: Verdict on this artifact if the released gate were enforced (Claude session bound to the run, Skill hook registered): 02 passes (its Skill call args carry the handoff path that `improve_call_since` matches); 05, 07, 12 are refused (no `improve` call recorded). But in 05/07/12 the model ran the runtime `done` (answer: 'This run is complete', state deleted) and `shiploop complete` in ONE shell call, so a refusal arrives after the loop is terminal; the handoff then says 'for complete status import its retained receipt without starting or reviewing again', so the 28.4 KB card is read and no review happens. The gate secures a call record, not a review. In 02 the call was made and the review was still a 26 s, 420-char note.
findings.proposal: Put the check before the runtime's `done` command exists: the 6.3 `improve-pass` verb calls `skill_calls.improve_call_since(root, since, tokens)` first and refuses with the existing text, reworded: 'Run the improve skill on this <stage> result first: no call to it has been recorded since this Improve stage started. Invoke the Skill tool with skill "improve" and args "ShipLoop Improve: <handoff>", let it finish its review, then run improve-pass again.' Keep the `complete` check as backstop. Same enforce conditions (`skill_gate`), so Grok and Codex stay ungated.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: host-neutral wording; enforcement stays Claude-only as D-24 accepts.
findings.risk: A model that types the runtime `done` by hand never calls `improve-pass`; the `complete` backstop still refuses with the post-hoc cost above. D-4 must hold: `improve-pass` prints `done`, it does not run it.
findings.plan_ref: 6.2 places the refusal in `complete`, after `done` has closed the loop; 6.3 `improve-pass` is the place before it; D-4
findings.est_effect: In this artifact 3 of 4 reviews: the card is read before the review instead of after a closed loop (about 85 KB read to no effect otherwise).

findings.where: shiploop_navigator.py `improve_start_contract` (passes `required_trivial_reviews=2` for every stage); skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/scripts/until_loop_ephemeral.py on branch -stop-; plan step 6.4 and D-6
findings.observation: Owner decision (stop rule for implement-step code reviews). This artifact cannot decide it: all 4 reviews ended on pass 1 (trivial, tree unchanged), the stop main's unchanged-first-pass rule (2be7906b) already gives; none edited anything, so no confirming pass ran. The deciding data is the Salesforce run (sfchess/live2 review files, read by me): 7 implement-step reviews, 5 ended at pass 1; ed863ab3 took 3 passes (P1 edit: a click before the list loaded threw; P2, P3 clean; the rule saves P3); adfd6e3b took 5 (P1 edit: inner-class fields private; P2 clean; P3 a real defect, 'Apex == on strings is case-insensitive' so black pieces were stored as white and black castling was lost; P4, P5 clean). The -stop- rule stops after P2 and cuts the P3 find; its lesson was cited by later reviews. Planning: the study's 8 material passes all precede their replay stop, and confirming passes after an edit found one non-material item.
findings.proposal: Planning stages (the five measured): 6.4 as built, one trivial pass with an unchanged measured tree. Step and last-item stages: stop on a first pass that leaves the tree unchanged (main's rule), but after any pass that edited require two consecutive passes that are trivial and leave the tree unchanged. Script-measured, no count or timer shown to the model. Implement: `improve_start_contract` picks the gate by the stage's improve kind in `stage_spec`; the vendored runtime accepts a second measured mode (the branch refuses gate values above 2; let 3 mean two consecutive measured clean passes), recorded in PROVENANCE like 6.4. Re-decide when the pass ledger (IMP-11) holds 10 step-stage reviews with at least 3 that edited code.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: selected by stage kind, no platform words; the evidence case is described by its language-semantics class, not by the sample.
findings.risk: A further vendored-runtime change inside the D-5 batch. n=2 multi-pass implement reviews in one Grok run, so the P3 find may be luck (the study's own limit). The extra pass costs only on reviews whose pass 1 edited code (2 of 7 live, 0 of 4 here).
findings.plan_ref: 6.4 and D-6 apply the rule to every Improve child; the branch journal's stop review F1 lists this option; the study says not to extend to code reviews
findings.est_effect: Keeps the planning saving (6 of 21 passes in the study); code reviews pay one extra pass (about 1 to 2 min live) only where pass 1 edited code; protects the one measured late code defect.

findings.observation: The verdict is written before the evidence exists: in 02, 05, 07 and 12 the `cat > reviews/review-1.md` with 'Nothing material ... trivial' sits in the same shell call that first gathers the evidence. Tree unchanged (`improve_changes.review_changes` returns no changed path): 'Tree unchanged since improve-bind (<tree12>); producer checks: RUN/tests/<file> (<n> ran, exit 0)'. Tree changed: rerun the stage's recorded check and focused commands and the lint on changed lines through the same `test_loop.verify` call the end-of-work branch of `_improve_change_gate` already makes, and write the exit codes. The model's own rows live in review-<n>.md only; 6.3's refusal of stale model-added rows stays.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: uses recorded commands and the bind snapshot, nothing platform-specific.
findings.risk: A recorded command that deploys or writes outside the tree must not rerun: use the same grants as the step and only the check/focused suites. Extra run time only on changed trees.

findings.where: shiploop_navigator.py `_item_commit`, `_PRODUCTS['verify']` row 'item commit', status `Done:` line; shiploop_item_scope.py `commit_item`
findings.observation: End-of-work review (12): the carry-forward result says 'W1 is committed' and ShipLoop prints it ('W1 closed: paginate fix and TC-1 committed'), but the worktree's `git log` shows only the seed and a docs commit and `git status` shows ` M src/paginate.js`, ` M test/paginate.test.js`. The review wrote 'Product changes are still uncommitted ... flagged for the parent', classed it trivial and satisfied; ShipLoop accepted and moved to system-test-author; nothing consumed the note. Verify's response has no 'ShipLoop committed W1' line, and verify's packet said 'No change inventory recorded for W1'; `commit_item` returns ('', []) silently when `changed_paths` is empty. The handoff names the commit only by pattern ('the WORKTREE commit whose subject starts feat: W1'), so a review must grep git. Probably seed-specific (the harness recorded the stages without a W1 base snapshot); not reproduced.
findings.proposal: Persist the item commit like `PREPARATORY_BASE`: `_item_commit` writes RUN/commits/<item>.md with the SHA or 'none: <reason>', and the 'item commit' product row prints 'commit <sha12> in WORKTREE' or 'none recorded (<reason>)'. `_item_commit` prints 'ShipLoop committed nothing for <item>: <reason>' when `commit_item` returns '' while the declared paths are dirty. Optional: fall back to `git status --porcelain` over the declared paths when no inventory exists. No directive to the review beyond reading the fact (no 'report unresolved': the review cannot commit).
findings.risk: Likely only visible in seeded or recovered runs; one more record to keep consistent (a fact, not a cursor).
findings.plan_ref: not in the plan; closest W7 script-owned fields (7.1)
findings.est_effect: The end-of-work review stops grepping git by subject; a silent no-commit becomes a printed, recorded fact before system tests and release.

findings.where: shiploop_keepalive.py `DRIVING_COMMAND`, `command_run_dir`, `observe`; plan step 6.3 `improve-pass`; W9 'hooks must see every command'
findings.observation: All 4 Improve tails re-typed the printed commands through shell variables: `R=...; P=...; SC=...; python3 $SC complete --run-dir=$R --action=...` (12 used `--run-dir=run`, relative). I ran the hook regexes: `DRIVING_COMMAND.search('python3 $SC complete --run-dir=$R ...')` is False and `command_run_dir` returns None; `observe` ignores a marker shown by a non-driving command, so such a call neither binds nor refreshes the run, and the Skill-call gate enforces only for a session the hooks bound. In 05, 07, 12 paths are 35%, 39%, 35% of the 2.0 to 2.4 KB the model writes per tail (140-char run dir).
findings.proposal: `improve-pass` prints the two commands it wants run (the runtime `done` and the `complete`), each literal, absolute and copy-ready, in one block; the handoff's last section repeats them. Add a test that `DRIVING_COMMAND` matches every command the Improve packet and `improve-pass` print. No regex change: a hook must not guess variables (KISS).
findings.risk: The model may still type variables; the visible symptom is a gate that does not enforce, so keep the one-time `note_not_enforced` line.
findings.plan_ref: 6.3 (register the verb in the hook verb sets), W9, principle 5 (hooks must see every command)
findings.est_effect: Model-written tail 2.0 to 2.4 KB to at most 1.0 KB (6.3 target 1.5 KB); keeps run binding intact.

findings.where: shiploop_navigator.py `_unchanged_first_pass`, `_derived_improve_receipt`; Run Review export; plan steps 1.3 and 8.5
findings.observation: The receipt does not record, per pass, what the stop-scope and gate decisions need. The data exist: the terminal packet's `progress` (`unchanged_first_pass`; `last_pass_changed_tree` on -stop-), review-file mtimes against `start.json`, `skill-calls.jsonl` timestamps. This artifact: 4 reviews took 55 s of 223 s (25%) and 12 tool calls of 70 turns; 4 of 4 labelled trivial, one of them (12) carrying an unresolved note.
findings.proposal: At import ShipLoop writes RUN/improve/<action>/passes.md and the Run Review export reads it: stage, pass n, label, measured tree changed (y/n), seconds (review-file mtime minus the previous mtime or `start.json`), skill call recorded (y/n/not enforced), focus ids answered (IMP-6). Print the decision rule beside it: re-decide IMP-4 at 10 step-stage reviews with at least 3 edits.
findings.risk: Low; one more derived file (rewritten from receipts, never a cursor).
findings.plan_ref: 1.3 (measurement of the whole reading path) and 8.5 (decision rule)
findings.est_effect: Turns the one-run stop-rule anecdote (7 implement reviews) into a per-release series.

works_well: The one-pass exit works as designed: all 4 reviews ended on pass 1 ('the first pass was trivial with the workspace unchanged'), ShipLoop imported each on the first `complete` and printed the next packet; no Improve refusal (artifact sections 02, 05, 07, 12).

ShipLoop owns the opening and the child start: in 4 of 4 reviews the model did not write an opening or start the runtime; it ran `done` then `complete`, and `_derived_improve_receipt` imported review-1.md and checks.md from the reviews directory with no model-listed paths.

The Improve packet is short and literal: 2,052 to 2,852 chars in the artifact (2.3 to 2.5 KB at main, about 0.9 KB of it the two steps); step 1 gives the exact Skill call and 02 copied it (skill-craft:improve with 'ShipLoop Improve: <handoff>'), which is what the gate's token match needs. The 'not from memory of an earlier one' clause already at main answers the 05/07/12 shortcut.
The end-of-work review is the one stage that looks at git after verify and noticed the uncommitted product diff (12); keep that look and make the fact script-owned (IMP-7).

History window plus 'Key learnings:' commits work when followed: in the Salesforce run later reviews cite earlier commit lessons (ed863ab3 review-1 cites fe238313 'Apex == ignores case'); the improve-commit lessons rule is worth keeping unchanged.

Reviews honestly record 'self-review (inline default)' with no claim of independence, as the binding requires; the duplicate-review gate was not tripped by the hand-varied texts (and is not the control that matters here).
not_measured: Whether the recorded run's hooks were bound: the build (1.3.0 / 2.3.1) predates the Skill-call hook, so the gate verdicts are read from `_skill_call_gate`, `skill_gate` and `improve_call_since`, not run live.

Cold-context behaviour (S-6): all four reviews ran in one warm session; whether a cleared model opens the handoff, invokes the skill unprompted or reads review-policy.md and ADAPTER.md is untested here.

Review depth on a defective input: no seeded defect, so pass-1 defect catch, and whether IMP-1/IMP-6/IMP-10 raise it, is not measured. A one-line fix leaves little to find, so 4 of 4 'none' is weak evidence of review quality either way.

Stop-rule effect on live time: the Salesforce passes were read by me from review text (materiality is my judgement, not analyst models'); the saving is a replay estimate, n=7 implement reviews in one Grok 4.7 medium run.
Whether the model shows the narrative block in Improve stages (no narrative appears in its tool-visible text; a host may display hook output separately).
Root cause of the missing `feat: W1` commit: read in `commit_item`, not reproduced; the harness seeding is the likely cause.
Handoff sizes were rendered at a short run directory; the artifact's 163-char prefix adds path text per occurrence and was not re-rendered.
The host's shell-output limit behind the 42 KB persisted-output (value unknown), and the per-turn latency split between reasoning and tools for the 26 s versus 6 s reviews.
